review_type: Independent source-constrained translation and lexical review; not a native-speaker or release acceptance

decision_semantics.retain: Keep this exact proposed wording after this independent static review. Does not certify runtime rendering, native preference, accessibility or release readiness.
decision_semantics.hold: Do not adopt this candidate. No replacement wording is accepted.
decision_semantics.revise: No row receives this outcome because no adequately supported replacement was established.

rows.fidelity: The same geometric word fits a round brush/line cap and a circular cursor marker. It adds no stroke-join promise and carries no numeric-rounding meaning in either menu.
rows.idiom: A compact shape label, independently attested in the identical line-cap context. Retain the unmodified value rather than making it brush-specific, because the resource is shared with the cursor control.
evidence: LO cui messages.po lines 13187–13191: nonfuzzy linetabpage|liststoreCAP_STYLE, Round → ክብ.
LibreOffice Insert Shape help lists ክብ among geometry labels; supplementary live corroboration only.

rows.fidelity: Names the SQUARE line cap and a square cursor-marker outline. Both consumers require geometry, not a square unit or exponent. The code keeps ROUND joins; this label need not and must not be expanded into a guarantee of square corners throughout the ink path.
rows.idiom: The supplied spelling is attested as both the line-cap option and a square graphic object. This supports retaining it, not claiming it is the uniquely preferred everyday/native term. I found no evidence here that warrants replacing it with an unverified geometry alternative.
evidence: LO cui messages.po lines 13193–13197: nonfuzzy linetabpage|liststoreCAP_STYLE, Square → ስኴር.
LO svx messages.po lines 103–107: nonfuzzy STR_ObjNameSingulQUAD, Square → ስኴር.
LibreOffice Insert Shape help lists ስኴር in the common-shape sentence.

confidence.lexical_match: high attestation, not independent native preference

rows.fidelity: ሰያፍ ጭረት describes orientation and a graphical mark, not the named calligraphic character/style. The Brush implementation stamps diagonal segments, but an implementation description cannot silently replace the English Calligraphy. Changing singular to plural would not restore the missing concept.
rows.idiom: Components are interpretable, but neither their compositional grammar nor their implementation fit establishes the Amharic term for a calligraphic brush. No exact replacement is accepted by this review.
evidence: LO svx messages.po lines 79–83 supports Diagonal line; Android pointer_stroke_style supports graphical stroke vocabulary, not Calligraphy.
ClassicPaintActivity.kt lines 785–788 restricts this third choice to Brush; PaintCanvas.kt lines 507–526 implements repeated diagonal strokes.
rows.next_step: Find or independently validate an Amharic term conveying the calligraphic style in a brush context. Retain the English source unless a genuine source defect is separately established; then follow English-first, all-affected-locales review.

rows.fidelity: In this three-choice shape-style control, Outline denotes the shape boundary without an interior fill. Border only is a faithful contextual rendering: only makes the exclusion already inherent in this Outline-versus-fill contrast explicit. Unlike fill only for Solid fill, it does not discard an independent modifier of the source.
rows.idiom: ድንበር is attested for a graphical control border rather than solely a national boundary, and ብቻ follows the noun naturally as a restrictive particle. The full phrase is an original composition, not an exact phrase certified by LibreOffice. Do not import ረቂቅ merely because another context has the English Outline.
evidence: LO help02.po lines 4312–4319: Border → ድንበር; following record describes a visible control frame.
LO cui messages.po lines 18591–18601 attests ብቻ in Only right/Only left.
PaintDocument.kt lines 271–282: style 0 skips the fill pass and draws the foreground stroke.

rows.fidelity: መሙያ ብቻ replaces solid/uniform fill with absence of an outline. The implemented option indeed lacks an outline, but that fact does not translate the source adjective solid. The paraphrase could describe non-solid patterned fill just as well and therefore loses source meaning.
rows.idiom: The submitted words are intelligible, but intelligibility and behavior contrast do not repair this fidelity gap. ሙሉ መሙያ is also not accepted: full/complete is not automatically the appropriate graphics sense of solid, and the supplied Solid record belongs to transparency rather than this shape-fill option.
evidence: LO svx messages.po lines 19823–19827 supports Fill → መሙያ.
LO svx messages.po lines 19955–20013 establishes that Solid → ሙሉ occurs inside a Transparency Type control.
PaintDocument.kt lines 271–282 fills style 1 with foreground and suppresses the outline; it does not make solid synonymous with only.
rows.next_step: Validate a wording that preserves solid/uniform fill as a graphics concept. Do not replace the English source with Fill only to rescue this translation. Any independently justified source change must precede an affected-languages review.

rows.fidelity: Both component nouns and the additive relationship are preserved. Here line is the shape border, not an instruction to fill a line. The English does not spell out foreground/background roles, so leaving those implicit is faithful rather than an omission introduced by translation.
rows.idiom: A concise noun-plus-noun UI label. The noun መሙያ matches a graphics-fill setting, and መስመር names a line; ASCII + and its surrounding spaces are preserved.
evidence: LO svx messages.po lines 19823–19827 supports Fill → መሙያ.
LO svx messages.po lines 61–65 supports graphic-object Line → መስመር.
PaintDocument.kt lines 271–282: style 2 uses background interior plus foreground stroke.

rows.fidelity: Names the geometry of the drawing-position marker. The code changes cursorShape and overrides the overlay cap independently of brushTip; the label must not be rewritten as Brush shape or Image shape.
rows.idiom: The genitive compound follows the Android የጠቋሚ pattern and uses the attested shape noun ቅርጽ. A graphical pointer term is appropriate here, unlike a text-caret-only term. No competing Amharic cursor vocabulary appears among the 12 supplied production entries; wider pending proposals were outside this review.
evidence: Android values-am/strings.xml lines 2020, 2077 and 5413 support pointer/stylus-pointer vocabulary paired with supplied English records.
LO svx messages.po lines 517–521 supports Shape → ቅርጽ.
ClassicPaintActivity.kt lines 1526–1538 uses this value as visible label and Spinner contentDescription. PaintCanvas.kt lines 292 and 371 passes independent cursorShape caps to the overlay.

consumer_qualification: The shape-style contrast is conditional on a fill-capable shape. Open Polygon dispatches as PaintTool.LINE for preview (PaintCanvas.kt:276) and commit (445); PaintDocument.drawShape excludes LINE/CURVE from interior fill and always strokes them. Do not claim that choosing Solid fill fills an open polygon. This qualification is not an English-source defect finding.
source_gate: No source change is proposed or silently incorporated. The two holds are translation-fidelity failures, not proof the English source is defective. If a source defect is later established, correct English, flag affected languages, then review them one by one.
evidence_quality: Primary localization records demonstrate usage, not correctness or native acceptance. Nonfuzzy means the record is not marked fuzzy; it is not a quality certification. Round and Square have exact same-domain evidence; the other retained phrases are component-based compositions. Full source files were inspected at the pinned snapshot, not an exhaustive repository-wide consumer search.
